results.conclusion: Key reveal delivers paid research by making the writer publish a decryption key through a validated EscrowFinish. The buyer receives encrypted delivery bytes first, but those bytes stay quarantined. Only after the engine verifies the successful finish, the key binding and the authenticated envelope can premium plaintext become accessible through a verified grant. Foundries and their largest customers have used advance payments for decades, particularly when a customer needs assurance that a new process node will be available in volume. The prepayment can cover a portion of the total contract value or the entire amount. It can be refundable or non-refundable, depending on the terms. Public disclosures rarely include the full contract, so the exact terms are often known only to the parties and their auditors. On 2026-08-14, the Open Records Desk reviewed public filings and company statements describing a common arrangement in the semiconductor supply chain: the wafer-capacity prepayment. Under this arrangement, a customer pays a foundry in advance for the right to receive a fixed volume of wafers at a future date. The payment is not a loan and not an equity investment. It is a contractual claim on manufacturing capacity. A prepayment secures future wafer capacity and is carried as a deposit until wafers are delivered. That single sentence, drawn from standard accounting guidance, is the core of the instrument.
